After one year, the average temperature would be around minus seventy-three degrees.
Back downtown, where it all began, everything would be still.
The palm trees frozen in place.
The cars white with frost.
Where the water used to move, a flat white plain.
No birds.
No traffic.
No sound at all.
But deep below that ice, the ocean would still be liquid.
Earth's own inner heat would keep the deep water from freezing for a very long time.
Near hot springs on the ocean floor, tiny life could carry on, never needing the Sun at all.
From far away, Earth would look like a dark, frozen marble.
And Earth itself would no longer circle anything.
Without the Sun's pull, it would fly off in a straight line, about thirty kilometers every second.
Every day, it would carry us more than two and a half million kilometers farther from where the Sun used to be.
Into the dark between the stars.
The stars would be brighter than you have ever seen them.
The Milky Way would stretch across the sky, sharper than on any night you have known.
Every bit of warmth you have ever felt came from one star.
And it would never come back.
